items.text: Part i: The graph shows that at 50 °C the solubility is 42.5g per 100g of water.

items.label: text
items.text: Part ii: From the graph we can see that the solubility at 40 °C is 40g per 100g of water. From this we can deduce that half as much, that is 20g, will dissolve in 50 g (half the mass) of water.

items.label: text
items.text: Part iii: Solubility measures the maximum mass of potassium chloride which will dissolve in 100 g of water at a particular temperature. Crystals will start to appear as soon as the solution becomes saturated. From the graph, it can be seen that more than 51.0g of solid will be soluble at 90°C, but as the solution is cooled the solubility decreases. Drawing a line across at 51.0g shows that this is the maximum mass that will dissolve at 80 °C and therefore crystals will first appear at temperatures below this.
